A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iJKOnet research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic energy-recovery experiments and iJKOnet results on Embryoid Body and Multiome data in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds energy-component comparisons, pairing sensitivity results, paired interaction recovery, and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The minimax objective, free-energy parameterization, transport-network approach, and Algorithm 1 are retained. Additional component combinations and discussion of initialization and stabilization experiments do not establish a change to the adopted algorithm.

E1.justification: Synthetic coverage extends to partially paired snapshots in Appendix A.3 and paired interaction-energy recovery in Appendix B.1.2. The underlying synthetic potentials, energy-recovery tasks, Embryoid Body data, and Multiome data remain covered.

E2.justification: The retained 5D comparison in Table 1 adds JKOnet* variants using V+U, V+W, W+U, and the full energy functional; v2 evaluated only its potential-only and time-varying-potential variants there. The non-JKO comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1.1 changes the stated samples per time step from 400 to 2000; B.1.2 changes them from 400/2000 to 2000/10000. New evaluations introduce a five-level pairing-fraction sweep and energy-component controls. These are substantial documented protocol revisions, without establishing reruns. EB time-label changes reflect reindexing; interaction sample counts remain inconsistent between B.1.2 and Figure 6.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds component ablations testing mixed and full energy parameterizations on cell data. Appendix A.3 adds a controlled pairing-fraction sensitivity study, and B.1.2 adds paired interaction recovery alongside the retained unpaired analysis. These substantially strengthen investigation of sampling dependence and energy-recovery failures.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies mini-batch Monte Carlo metric estimation and an unbiased finite-sample MMD estimator, whereas v2 provided population-level metric definitions. Existing three-run reporting and variability displays remain; no increase in runs or new significance testing is stated.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include pairing sensitivity, paired interaction recovery, component scores, and Table 7 timings. For example, Table 1 newly reports full-energy iJKOnet at 3.577±0.166 versus JKOnet* at 1.361±0.257 for t1. Diffusion-error boxplots also change between v2 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 7. Retained table entries remain numerically unchanged after matching reordered columns and time labels.

T1.justification: v3 adds convexity to the global assumption on X and corrects the ground-truth transport-map term in the proof from v2 Equation (28) to v3 Equation (29). Theorem 3.1, its bound, and the substantive proof strategy remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Section 6 now explicitly presents iJKOnet as a framework for recovering any type of energy functional, qualified by the implemented free-energy parameterization. The abstract and introduction retain the same central methodological, theoretical, and performance contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations that optimizing one shared energy functional regularizes training and that entropy-estimation difficulties cause diffusion-recovery failures. Section 5.2 also introduces a DMSB speed-advantage interpretation based on timings from different dimensions. The principal applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The promised code release becomes explicit repository and README access information. Appendix C adds metric-estimation sample counts, POT usage, MMD kernel and bandwidth choices, Optuna tuning information, and initialization/stabilization details. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to all underlying settings.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands coverage of neural OT, barycenters, bridge matching, WeightFlow, dynamics from stationary distributions, and tensor-train approaches. Section 3.4 additionally distinguishes energy-recovery guarantees from Wu and Wang's density-convergence analysis. This exceeds a limited citation update.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section order remain stable. Local revisions clarify the loss derivation, evaluation descriptions, and training discussion; v3 also adds reproducibility and acknowledgments paragraphs and updates affiliations, headers, and cross-references.

P2.justification: v3 adds the pairing-sensitivity and paired-interaction figures, expands and groups Table 1, introduces timing Table 7, reorders Table 4 columns, and redesigns the diffusion-error plot. Existing potential and unpaired-interaction plots are retained under new figure numbers.

improvement.justification: The new component and pairing ablations strengthen evidence about when iJKOnet succeeds or fails, while code-access instructions and concrete metric details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by conflicting interaction sample counts in Appendix B.1.2 versus Figure 6 and a new DMSB runtime claim based on different dimensions. Overall, support and transparency improve, but the reporting weaknesses limit the gain.
